summary: Console alerts suppressed for LumaChat org during us-east failover; tracehook links missing in restored dashboards
description: Issue summary: During an automated failover of the us-east ingestion cluster on 2026-03-10 03:15 UTC, LumaChat (dedicated customer) observed a multi-hour window where console alerts for surge/error-rate thresholds were not firing and dashboard tracehook links were either missing or pointing to stale tokens. Impact: Customer missed one high-severity outage (inference error-rate spike) which should have paged on-call. Several dashboard widgets showed zeroed alert counts during the backfill window.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Simulate regional failover by demoting ingest-leader in prod-us-east (internal runbook)
2) Trigger a synthetic high error-rate workload scoped to LumaChat org
3) Observe alert evaluation logs and dashboard tracehook tokens during backfill/rehydration window
4) Note that alert evaluations are suppressed if tracehook token resolution returns null for org-scoped attributes
logs_and_evidence:
- Alert eval logs: eval-runner/us-east: 2026-03-10T03:22:01Z: WARN suppressed-eval: org_attr_lookup returned null for org=lumachat
- Ingest backfill job: backfill-controller: 2026-03-10T03:40:12Z: INFO rehydration-start: 12 partitions queued
- Dashboard snapshot: widget 'Error Rate (5m)' shows zero counts between 03:20-06:10 UTC; tracehook URL parameter token= null
- PagerDuty incident: PD-98721 (customer reported missed page), Slack thread: #support-lumachat <https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C040X9Y1E/p167852...>
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: backfill dedup/compaction step marked recent events as already-processed which caused alert eval runner to skip this org during the window.
Findings:
- org-attribute cache (org-attr-service) was briefly returning 503 during the failover while state transfer completed; alert-eval had a defensive fast-fail path that treats missing org attributes as 'suppress eval' to avoid false positives. This combined with the backfill dedupe window caused alerts to be neither evaluated (suppressed) nor queued for re-evaluation.
- Tracehook token generation relies on the org-attr-service for per-org signing keys; when org-attr-service returned errors, tracehook generation returned an empty token and dashboard links dropped the tracehook param.
- Backfill rehydration later rewrote metrics without restoring alert-eval watermark metadata, so no catch-up evaluation occurred.
- Related internal issue INT-4021 tracks an intermittent zero-return bug in org-attr-service during leader election.
customer_communication:
2026-03-10 04:05 UTC: Acknowledge receipt to customer (Aisha) - we are investigating and will provide ETA.
2026-03-10 07:30 UTC: Sent interim update explaining regional failover sequence and immediate workaround (manual re-run of alert-eval for affected org).
Customer requested postmortem and confirmation of pages that were missed.
workarounds:
1) Manual trigger: run alert-eval re-evaluate_job --org=lumachat --range=2026-03-10T03:00:00Z/2026-03-10T07:00:00Z (SRE only)
2) Temporarily disable 'suppress-on-missing-org-attr' guard in eval-runner config for dedicated tiers until org-attr-service SLA restored (requires careful risk review)
3) For dashboards, re-generate tracehook tokens via: admin-console -> Org Keys -> Regenerate for LumaChat (short-term; tokens will change)
resolution:
Mitigation completed 2026-03-11 02:10 UTC: SRE ran a targeted re-evaluation job for LumaChat (range 03:00-07:00 UTC) which retroactively fired alerts and created corresponding alert history entries. Tracehook tokens were regenerated for the org and dashboards were refreshed.
Permanent fix planned: PR #1189 updates eval-runner to queue re-evaluation when org-attr-service returns transient errors instead of silently suppressing; PR #1192 ensures backfill jobs also restore evaluation watermark metadata.
Follow-ups: schedule postmortem (link below), add synthetic test in chaos-suite that simulates org-attr unavailability during failover, and add a Grafana alert for org-attr error-rate spikes.
